item.title: BIONICLE: Re: BIONICLE
item.content:encoded:
I vaguely remember Makuta in the second movie being too campy for me to take seriously. Roodaka scared the living daylights out of me as a kid though, especially in the scene where she's talking to Vakama about how loyal her horde is. She straight-up tells a bunch of visorak to jump off a tower and they immediately do just that and that scarred me a bit as a kid.

they were all far better than any toy-inspired direct-to-video animated movie has any right to be.

This. They had visorak blink independently and even had a janitor visorak cleaning the floor in the foreground of one of the scenes. It's insane how well-animated the movies are for that time.

item.title: BIONICLE: Re: BIONICLE
item.content:encoded:
I remember getting Roodaka and being so stoked at how many parts she had, so I could make more beautiful creations. I also watched one of the moves, but never got too terrible into the lore.

I remember the Bionicle movies being unusually good for the time—especially the third movie, Web of Shadows. Roodaka's voice actor did an amazing job as the Queen of the Visorak. The other two movies were alright; though not as memorable as the third I felt.

item.title: SCP D and D campaign: Re: SCP D and D campaign
item.content:encoded:
I've been thinking about this too, and I think the GOC might actually be a better group for the party to be a member of than the Foundation. It seems like the GOC employs magic-users, arcane and divine, more than the Foundation does, and they're also more focused on combating and destroying anomalies than capturing them, as are most D&D parties. There's not much fun about Nine-Tailed Fox sweeping up after a breach or the Mole Rats getting picked off in another endless underground tunnel, but a GOC party can just roll up and start killing shit.

For extra fun, set it in an SCP-5000 scenario, where the Foundation has gone crazy and evil and is spewing rampaging, highly killable anomalies all over the place. Defend Ganzir, try to protect civilian populations, destroy Foundation Sites, team up with the CotBG, or even try to retrieve SCP-055 and bring it to SCP-579, assuming that Pietro Wilson failed in this timeline.
